entry.title: How our forecast is made, and how to read it
entry.summary: When will a law that is still being negotiated be in the Official Journal? Our forecast answers with what comparable EU laws actually took, not with plans. This memo explains where it comes from, how it works, how often it was right in the past and what it cannot know.

entry.title: The forecast for statisticians: estimand, algorithm, evaluation and limits
entry.summary: A technical note on our forecast of EU legislative procedures: a conditional, non-parametric reference class forecast with a size neighbourhood and a calendar transformation. Evaluated out of sample with PIT, interval coverage and the CRPS, including a check for look-ahead in our own backtest. What holds up, what does not, and where we would welcome advice.

entry.title: Large laws take longer: our forecast now compares like with like
entry.summary: We tested which properties of a proposal go with how long the EU takes to adopt it. Size wins clearly; commas, consultations and the State of the Union address do not. Since 13 October the forecast compares each file with files of similar size, and most dates move later.
